transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I came in today because things have just taken a really sharp turn for me lately. I manage production at an industrial plant, and for a while, I was doing a lot. I mean, I was launching nonstop plant redesign projects, calling our suppliers way after hours, and basically rewriting the entire shift plan all by myself. I just had all this drive to get things done. 

But then... I don't know, I just hit a wall. Suddenly, I'm completely unable to keep up with the very plans I just set in motion. I went from doing everything to barely being able to manage what I started, and I really need to figure out what's going on.
Have you experienced periods where your mood was unusually elevated, irritable, or you felt extremely confident or energetic, not just increased drive to get things done?

Yes, I did. Um, when I first started this assignment, I felt almost... electrically upbeat. Just incredibly energized and on top of the world. 

But then it kind of shifted into me being weirdly irritable. Like, if anyone questioned my ideas or the plans I was making, I got really annoyed. It just felt like they were slowing down something that was obvious and important. So, yeah, it definitely went beyond just wanting to get things done.
After you hit that wall and things slowed down, did you feel persistently sad, lose interest in activities, or experience other symptoms of depression?

Yes, it's been really hard. Lately, I wake up in my temporary apartment with this heavy, hollow feeling. It's just... it feels like the day is already ruined before I even drive to the plant. I just feel so down all the time now.

Have you ever experienced a period where your mood was elevated or irritable for at least 4 consecutive days, along with other changes like decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, or being more talkative than usual?

Yes, definitely. During that time when I was making all those plans, the sleep thing was really noticeable. I was sleeping maybe two, sometimes three hours a night at most. But the weird part was, I didn't feel tired. I'd still show up at the plant the next morning feeling totally sharp and charged up. It honestly felt like sleep was just... optional, you know? Like it was just an inefficient use of my time when I had so much to do. So yeah, I was definitely running on almost no sleep for days in a row.

During that time when you felt so energized and were sleeping very little, did you also experience racing thoughts, being more talkative than usual, or taking on too many projects or activities that were risky or out of character for you?

Yes, I was definitely more talkative. Um, in our meetings at the plant, I could actually hear myself talking faster and... just longer than usual. I would jump right from discussing line speeds to staffing, and then straight into supplier issues, all before anyone else could really even respond.
How long did you feel that way — when you were sleeping very little, talking more than usual, and jumping from one idea to another? Was it just a few days, or did it last longer?

Honestly, I'm not exactly sure. It's a little hard to pin down the exact number of days because I wasn't really keeping track of time while it was happening. It definitely felt like a continuous stretch, but I couldn't tell you for sure if it was just a few days or if it went on longer than that. It's all just a bit of a blur now.
Looking back, do you think the time when you felt that way — sleeping very little, talking more, and jumping from idea to idea — lasted for at least a full week?

I really can't say if it was a full week. Like I said, I wasn't keeping track, and it's hard to remember exactly when it started or stopped. It was definitely a stretch of days, but I just don't know if it hit the seven-day mark.
Did you experience any time where you felt unusually high, irritable, or energized for a full week or more, even if it wasn’t every single day?

Well, when I first started this assignment, I definitely had this stretch where I felt... almost electrically upbeat. Just full of energy. But then it kind of shifted, and I got weirdly irritable. It was like... if anyone questioned my ideas at the plant, I felt like they were just slowing down something that was obvious and important. But again, I just don't know if that specific feeling lasted a full week or more. It's hard to put an exact timeframe on it.
Can you recall if the time when you felt unusually energized, irritable, or high lasted for at least 7 days straight without a significant break?

I... I really don't know. I know you're trying to get a specific number of days out of me, but I just can't give you one. It was a continuous stretch, yes, but whether it was exactly seven days straight without a break? I honestly couldn't tell you. I wasn't marking it on a calendar.
Looking back, can you confirm whether the time you felt unusually energized, irritable, or high lasted for at least 4 full days in a row without a significant break?

Yeah, four days... yes. I can definitely say it was at least four days in a row. Like I said, I don't know if it made it to a full week, but it was absolutely a solid four or five days where I was just running on that high energy and not needing sleep. There wasn't any break in it during that specific window.

During that time when you felt unusually energized or irritable, did you also notice any other changes in your behavior or thinking, such as feeling overly confident, being easily distracted, or taking on more tasks than you could handle?

Yeah, I definitely noticed a change in how I was thinking. I mean, I honestly believed I could fix the entire production workflow at the plant all by myself, and do it faster than the whole consulting team we had hired. I was just so sure of myself. People tried to bring up concerns or point out issues with my plans, but I completely brushed them off. At the time, failing didn't even seem like a possibility to me. I just felt like I knew exactly what needed to be done and no one else could see it.

During the time you felt unusually energized or irritable, did you experience at least three of the following: inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, more talkative than usual, racing thoughts, being easily distracted, increased goal-directed activity, or excessive involvement in risky activities?

Well, going by that list... yeah, I'd say I had at least three. I mean, I already told you earlier about not needing sleep. And just now I mentioned being overly confident and taking on the whole plant workflow, which I guess covers the inflated self-esteem and the increased goal-directed activity. 

So that's three right there. As for the other things you mentioned—like racing thoughts or risky activities—I'm really not sure. I didn't really notice anything like that. But I definitely had the three I just said.
During that same time when you felt so energized and irritable, did you notice yourself being more distracted than usual or having thoughts that were racing faster than normal?

Um, no, like I... like I just mentioned a second ago, I didn't really notice my thoughts racing. And as for being distracted... no, I don't think so. 

Honestly, if anything, I was hyper-focused. I was completely zeroed in on that workflow project at the plant. I wasn't really bouncing around from thing to thing or losing my train of thought. I was just intensely focused on that one big plan I had. So, no, neither of those really fit.
Looking back, can you confirm whether the time you felt unusually energized, irritable, or high lasted for at least 7 full days in a row without a significant break?

No, it didn't last that long. It was only about four or five days, I think. Definitely not a full week. I just remember it starting around a Tuesday and by the weekend, I was already crashing hard into... well, feeling really down again. So, no, not seven days in a row.

Since you started feeling down after that period of high energy, have you experienced any additional symptoms of depression, such as losing interest in things you usually enjoy, changes in appetite or weight, trouble concentrating, or thoughts of death or suicide?

Well, out of those... the appetite thing is definitely an issue. My eating is just all over the place right now. 

Some days I'll look at the clock and realize it's 4 p.m. and literally all I've had is coffee. I just completely forget to eat. But then other nights, I'll be standing in the kitchen just eating takeout straight from the container, even though I'm not actually hungry at all. It's just very erratic. 

As for the other stuff you mentioned... losing interest or the trouble concentrating... I'm really just noticing the eating changes the most right now.
Since you started feeling down after that high-energy period, have you had trouble concentrating or focusing on your work at the plant?

Yes, definitely. It's been really bad lately. Like, just the other day we had this shift-planning meeting, and... I just couldn't hold the staffing numbers in my head. I couldn't even keep track of them long enough to make a really basic decision. It's honestly terrifying, because organizing that kind of stuff is exactly my job, and I just couldn't do it.
